front: Trigger: "every window of size k," "k consecutive items"
back: Fixed window. Add the entering item, remove the leaving item. O(n).

front: Trigger: "a block that's a rearrangement of s1"
back: Fixed window of counts, size len(s1). Compare counts each slide.

front: Trigger: "longest substring / subarray that follows a rule"
back: Variable window, longest valid. Grow right, shrink left while broken, record after.

front: Trigger: "you may change / flip up to k items"
back: Restate as a window with at most k bad items. Count the bad items; shrink when over k.

front: Trigger: "shortest / minimum window that satisfies X"
back: Variable window, shortest valid. Grow right; while valid, record then shrink.

front: Trigger: "contains all characters of t"
back: Shortest valid window with need/have counts. Valid when have == required.

front: Trigger: "all words, same length, concatenated in any order"
back: Window of word-sized pieces, run once per offset 0..L−1.

front: Subarray sums with negative numbers: sliding window?
back: No. Shrinking might raise the sum, so the window can't tell which way to move. Use prefix sums + hashmap (Section 05).

front: Write the fixed-window loop
Write the LONGEST-valid template
back: Shrink while broken. Record after the while.

front: Write the SHORTEST-valid template
back: Record inside the while, before shrinking.

front: Longest vs shortest: three differences
back:
• while runs when broken / when valid
  • record after / inside the while
  • best starts at 0 / at infinity

front: Window length from left and right
back: right - left + 1. Indexes 2..5 hold 4 items. (M5)

front: Why is the variable window O(n) with a while inside a for?
back: left only moves forward: at most n moves total. right moves n times. ≤ 2n steps. (Amortized.)

front: LC 643 Maximum Average Subarray I — key idea
back:
• Fixed window of k; slide with + entering − leaving
  • Track the best sum, divide by k at the end
  • O(n), O(1)

front: LC 567 Permutation in String — key idea
back:
• Window of len(s1) over s2; 26-slot counts
  • Match when window counts == s1 counts
  • O(26n)

front: LC 3 Longest Substring Without Repeating — key idea
back:
• Set of window letters; while s[right] in set: remove s[left], left += 1
  • Or: last-index dict, left = max(left, last[c] + 1)
  • O(n)

front: LC 3: why max(left, last[c] + 1) and not just last[c] + 1?
back: The old copy may already be left of the window. Without max, left jumps backward. Trace "abba".

front: LC 1004 Max Consecutive Ones III — key idea
back:
• Longest window with ≤ k zeros
  • Count zeros; shrink while zeros > k
  • O(n)

front: LC 424 Longest Repeating Character Replacement — key idea
back:
• Changes = length − max letter count
  • Shrink while changes > k
  • 26-slot counts: O(26n)

front: LC 209 Minimum Size Subarray Sum — key idea, trap
back:
• Shortest valid: while sum ≥ target, record then shrink
  • Trap: return 0 if nothing works
  • Needs positives only

front: LC 76 Minimum Window Substring — when does have change?
back:
• +1 when a letter's window count reaches need
  • −1 when it drops below need
  • Record start and length, return the slice

front: LC 30 Substring with Concatenation — key idea
back:
• Pieces of length L; one run per offset 0..L−1
  • Not a word → reset; too many of a word → shrink
  • Full window → record left

front: Fixed window: which index leaves when nums[right] enters?
back: nums[right - k]. Trace it once on a small example. (M5)

front: Variable window: if or while to shrink?
back: while. One step left may not fix the window. Keep shrinking until valid. (Lab 3.09; candidate M9.)

front: Shortest window: what if nothing is ever valid?
back: best is still infinity. Return 0 (or ""). Read the no-answer case. (M6)

front: Why does Minimum Size Subarray Sum need positive numbers?
back: Growing must raise the sum and shrinking must lower it. Negatives break that.

front: Counter comparison trap with hand-written dicts
back: {a: 1, b: 0} vs {a: 1} may not compare equal. Delete zero keys or use a 26-slot list.

front: Brute force for longest substring: why is "extend each start" O(n²)?
back: With many different characters, each start can run far before a repeat. n starts × long runs.
